title: Ground truth for XNPV5 at 12/31/1996 (B41) and 12/31/2000 (B42) is hardcoded from an undisclosed monthly schedule and discounts to 1/31/1997 and 1/31/2001 instead of 12/31/1996 and 12/31/2000
evidence: In problem.py, the task asks the agent to fill in the annual table for 1997–2019 and 'Finally, provide the equity present value (XNPV5) as of 12/31/1996 and 12/31/2000.' In gt_43_ref_0.xlsx ('Damage Calculations' cells B41 and B42), the reference values are stored as static hardcoded floats with no formulas (f=None): B41 = 586133469.49314284 ($586,133,469) and B42 = 548419739.23546267 ($548,419,739). These exact float64 figures come from running XNPV(0.05, values, dates) on an unprovided 276-month (Jan 1997–Dec 2019) and 228-month (Jan 2001–Dec 2019) schedule of Monthly Capacity Payments (G39:AC39 repeated 12 times per year) at calendar month-end dates (1/31/1997..12/31/2019 and 1/31/2001..12/31/2019) WITHOUT including the valuation dates 12/31/1996 and 12/31/2000. This creates two defects: (1) Undisclosed convention/ambiguity: the workbook only has annual columns (1997–2019 in G28:AC28) and contains no monthly schedule or date cells anywhere, nor does the prompt state whether XNPV5 is computed on the annual Yearly Capacity Payments (G38:AC38, giving $570,683,244.08 and $533,963,700.07 with year-end dates, or $570,855,996.25 and $534,096,889.71 via standard annual NPV) or on expanded monthly cash flows at month-end dates. (2) Invalid golden solution: because Excel's XNPV discounts to dates[0] (the first date in the series), passing dates starting at 1/31/1997 and 1/31/2001 without a 0-cash-flow anchor on 12/31/1996 and 12/31/2000 discounts the streams to 1/31/1997 and 1/31/2001 instead of 12/31/1996 and 12/31/2000, overstating the true monthly EOM XNPV as of 12/31/1996 ($583,709,662.01) and 12/31/2000 ($546,151,887.40) by a factor of 1.05^(31/365) (+$2,423,807.48 and +$2,267,851.84). Because grader_guidance uses binary single-score grading ('score': 0 or 1) and requires all values to be logically equivalent to the reference workbook (with numeric tolerance restricted 'only to web-search tasks'), a competent agent computing true XNPV/NPV as of 12/31/1996 and 12/31/2000 will differ by $2.3M–$15.5M from the hardcoded reference numbers and fail.
confirmation: GT 'Damage Calculations'!B41/B42 are hardcoded 586,133,469 and 548,419,739, which I reproduce exactly only as XNPV of the row-39 monthly payments at month-end dates with the first flow (1/31/1997, 1/31/2001) as base. Anchored at 12/31/1996 and 12/31/2000 they are 583.7M and 546.2M, and the input has
fix: gt_43_ref_0.xlsx 'Damage Calculations'!B41: 586,133,469.49 -> 583,709,662.01 and B42: 548,419,739.24 -> 546,151,887.40 (hardcoded values, as before). New values are XNPV at 5% (actual/365) of the row-39 monthly payments at month-ends Jan 1997 (Jan 2001) to Dec 2019, discounted to 12/31/1996 and 12/31/2000. The old values were reproduced exactly as the same flows discounted to the first payment date. No other cell changes and nothing references B41/B42. prompt.md: 'Finally, provide the equity present value (XNPV5) as of 12/31/1996 and 12/31/2000.' -> 'Finally, provide the equity present value (XNPV5) as of 12/31/1996 and 12/31/2000, discounting each Monthly Capacity Payment at 5% from its month-end date back to the valuation date.' (states the monthly month-end convention that the workbook does not reveal).

title: GT XNPV values are discounted to the first payment date, not to the 12/31/1996 and 12/31/2000 dates the task asks for
evidence: The task asks for 'the equity present value (XNPV5) as of 12/31/1996 and 12/31/2000', and the GT labels in A41/A42 read 'XNPV5 at 12/31/96' and 'XNPV5 at 12/31/00'. GT B41 = 586,133,469.49 and B42 = 548,419,739.24 are hardcoded values. I rebuilt them from GT row 39 (monthly payments, 276 month-end flows from 1/31/1997 to 12/31/2019). Both match exactly only when Excel's XNPV uses the first cash-flow date as the base: 1/31/1997 for B41 and 1/31/2001 for B42. Discounting the same flows to the stated dates at 5% (actual/365) gives 583,709,662 at 12/31/96 and 546,151,887 at 12/31/00. That is about 0.41% lower, or $2.4M and $2.3M. Other timing conventions also miss the key: beginning-of-month flows give 586,010,613 and 548,304,718; annual year-end flows give 570,683,244 and 533,963,700. The grader is binary (score 0/1) and asks whether the values are 'logically equivalent to the reference'. These two cells are the headline answers, so an agent that correctly discounts to the stated valuation dates can be failed.
confirmation: Recomputed from GT row 39: XNPV at 5% over 276/228 month-end flows equals B41/B42 only when based on 1/31/1997 and 1/31/2001, versus 583,709,662 and 546,151,887 when discounted to the 12/31/96 and 12/31/00 dates the prompt and labels A41/A42 ask for, so a correct answer differs from the key by about
fix: gt_43_ref_0.xlsx 'Damage Calculations'!B41: 586,133,469.49 -> 583,709,662.01 and B42: 548,419,739.24 -> 546,151,887.40 (hardcoded values, as before). New values are XNPV at 5% (actual/365) of the row-39 monthly payments at month-ends Jan 1997 (Jan 2001) to Dec 2019, discounted to 12/31/1996 and 12/31/2000. The old values were reproduced exactly as the same flows discounted to the first payment date. No other cell changes and nothing references B41/B42.
